body:
Is there a problem if `mulitpart/form-data` is used? It defaults to that encoding as the various parts don't know if there are files hiding in the payload and defaults to a value that will always be safe.

I think changing the docs here might be the simplest thing unless there is an issue with defaulting to `multipart/form-data`.

It might be safe to use multipart/form-data for POST requests (if the docs get updated), but an underlying problem with the Stream adapter is that it switches to multipart regardless of what method is being used. So if you make a PUT request and feed it an array (as in the documentation example that @dakota cited), it ends up getting submitted as multipart PUT request.

This is a problem, because PHP (on the receiving end) doesn't know how to handle that, and it may not even be legal under the HTTP spec: https://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=55815

I've got two Cake apps (one is a RESTful API, and the other is a web app that needs to talk to it). If I use Cake's HTTP client to make a PUT request to the API (and pass it an array as in the documentation's example), the API's $this->request->data is empty. For the moment, I'm working around this by wrapping my data array in http_build_query() before sending it to \Cake\Network\Http\Client::put().

> If I use Cake's HTTP client to make a PUT request to the API (and pass it an array as in the documentation's example), the API's $this->request->data is empty

@lorenzo If you remember similar issue came up in IRC too few days ago. Should we add some magic in RequestHandler to populate request->data for PUT requests too to overcome PHP's limitations?
@ADmad I think this is a completely different think. But actually we already decode form data (not multipart) into request->data
I can look into checking the request payload to see if there are any files before defaulting to multipart/form-data. Would that help solve the problems here?

Yes, that would be great. Also, in \Cake\Network\Http\Adapter\Stream::_buildContent() please check to make sure that the switch to multipart/form-data only occurs when $request->method() == Request::METHOD_POST, because the PUT method uses a different mechanism for uploading a file: http://php.net/manual/en/features.file-upload.put-method.php (although the data is not passed as an array in that case).
@davehensley That example is a bit oversimplified, as it doesn't account for file + non-file parameters which again needs multi-part/form-data from what I remember.

Everything I'm reading suggests that multipart/form-data is not intended to be used with PUT (i.e. if you want to combine file+non-file parameters you are supposed to use POST instead). cURL/Guzzle/etc. don't support it on the client side, and PHP itself doesn't support it on the receiving side.

http://www.lornajane.net/posts/2008/accessing-incoming-put-data-from-php#comment-809
https://github.com/appdotnet/api-spec/issues/281
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/guzzle/NDt0av_fRlU
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15106849/curl-php-uploading-files-with-put-request-how-do-i-process-this

My suggestion would be to avoid this behavior entirely, or at the very least, to make sure that multipart/form-data is NOT used when a file-only PUT request is made.

From the guzzle thread, guzzle now supports multipart/form-data requests with PUT, so I see no reason not to support it. We'll continue to bound by the limitation of needing to fit all fileuploads in PHP memory, but that isn't new.

issue.title: Fix Http\Client always using multipart/form-data as a content-type

issue.body:
Unless there are files, request bodies should be urlencoded, and not multipart/form-data. This increase compatibility with servers built with PHP. Only when files are included should the default type be set to
multipart/form-data.

I'm opening this against 3.1 as I think it represents enough of a behavior change that we should not include it in a bugfix release.

Refs #6840
